Work Permit

Working legally in the U.S. is essential for stability and peace of mind. Our immigration team in Florida helps you apply or renew your work permit (EAD) with accuracy and confidence, ensuring every step meets USCIS requirements.

Whether you’re in Miami or Orlando, our specialists handle your case carefully, preparing the necessary forms and guiding you until approval. We make the entire process smooth, fast, and stress-free.

From Tampa to Fort Lauderdale, our experienced immigration professionals assist clients across Florida with work authorization applications for different visa categories and situations.

What is the work permit service?

The work permit, officially known as the Employment Authorization Document (EAD), allows noncitizens to work legally in the U.S. It’s a vital document for immigrants waiting for residency, asylum, or visa approval.

Our immigration office in Florida assists with Form I-765 preparation, submission, and follow-up. We ensure your application is complete, accurate, and ready for USCIS processing without unnecessary delays.

This service helps you secure lawful employment while maintaining compliance with U.S. immigration laws and deadlines.

What benefits do you receive by hiring this service?

Choosing our immigration specialists in Florida for your work permit ensures efficiency, accuracy, and peace of mind throughout the process.

  • Expert preparation of Form I-765
  • Verification of eligibility and category
  • Review of all required documents
  • Fast and accurate USCIS submission
  • Updates on case status and approval notice
  • Bilingual assistance in English and Spanish
  • Renewal reminders for future permits

With professional support, your work authorization is handled with care, helping you avoid mistakes and delays that could affect your employment.

How does the work permit process work?

Understanding the process helps you stay prepared and ensures your application moves forward smoothly with USCIS.

  1. Eligibility check and document preparation
  2. Completion and filing of Form I-765
  3. Payment of fees and submission to USCIS
  4. Receipt notice and case number assignment
  5. Biometrics appointment (if required)
  6. Approval and EAD card delivery by mail

Each step is carefully managed by our immigration team to ensure compliance and timely approval of your work permit.

What should you know before applying for a work permit?

Before applying, make sure you know your EAD category and gather all necessary documents, including proof of identity and eligibility.

If you are renewing, file early to avoid gaps in work authorization. Our team helps you complete every form accurately and stay updated on USCIS requirements.

Being prepared and guided by professionals ensures your application is approved without stress or delays.

FAQ

Here are the most common questions about work permits in Florida, answered simply to help you understand the process.

Who can apply for a work permit?

Noncitizens with pending immigration cases, such as asylum, adjustment of status, or certain visas, can apply for work authorization.

How long does it take to receive the work permit?

Most EAD applications take between 3 and 6 months to process, depending on USCIS workload and category type.

Can I renew my work permit before it expires?

Yes, you can apply up to six months before expiration to avoid interruptions in your work eligibility.

What happens if my EAD expires?

You must stop working until your new card is approved. Timely renewal prevents employment interruptions.

Do I need a lawyer to apply?

It’s not required, but professional help ensures all forms and documents are complete and accurate, preventing USCIS rejections.

Can I change jobs with my work permit?

Yes, most EAD holders can change employers freely while their authorization is valid.

What documents do I need?

Passport, visa copy, I-94, two photos, and proof of eligibility such as pending case receipts or specific visa status.

Can I travel with my work permit?

No, the EAD is not a travel document. You’ll need advance parole or another valid permit to travel abroad legally.

If your question wasn’t answered, contact our immigration team today to receive personalized guidance for your work permit in Florida.
